name: security-gcp-cloudbuild-trigger-trust-review
intent: Cloud Build trigger/source trust and build service-account delegation
artifacts: Trigger event/source rules, build config substitution, service account, approvals and output artifact.
trace: Trace lower-trust source/config/variables into a build running with deployment or secret authority and ensure approval is bound to the actual revision.
experiment: Use an isolated owned build fixture with inert output; compare trusted release and a lower-trust source/config change.
disproof: A build service-account name in config is not usable authority if trigger/approval controls reject the untrusted run.
repair: Bind trusted source and approvals to execution, scope build identity and verify legitimate publication.
branch_decisions: Bind trigger source/ref, configuration file location and build service account. A trigger editor may indirectly control privileged build execution even without a direct service-account token. Inspect approval and repository-connection boundaries; do not infer that a PR can select a privileged account merely because a configuration field names it.
operational_method: Identify trigger creator/editor, required iam.serviceAccounts.actAs authority, configured trigger build account and actual worker execution account. Retain the resolved source/ref and build configuration from the admitted trigger run. A service-account name in untrusted YAML is only a request until platform admission accepts it. The local model must preserve the account-selection gate, and a denied trigger edit must not become a claim that the worker executed under that account.
